differentiation.support: Provide the student notes open at the proton and nucleon number definitions so learners can follow the subtraction for neutrons before counting electrons.

differentiation.stretch: Ask learners to explain why alpha particles mostly passed straight through gold foil before they take the exit ticket.

assessmentPoints: Shell-model answers in the opening activity
Trap answers in the sixth activity and the closing worksheet
successCriteria: I can name the nucleus as the tiny dense centre holding the protons and neutrons
I can say electrons sit in fixed shells and the atom is mostly empty space
objectives.text: Describe the atom: a tiny dense nucleus of protons and neutrons, with electrons in shells around mostly empty space

assessmentPoints: Carbon answers in the second activity
Sodium answers in the third activity and the closing worksheet
successCriteria: I can read the proton number as the number of protons and give a neutral atom the same number of electrons
I can work out neutrons as nucleon number minus proton number, such as 23 - 11 = 12 for sodium
objectives.text: Count protons, neutrons and electrons from the proton and nucleon numbers

assessmentPoints: Group answers in the fourth activity
Period answers in the fifth activity and the closing exit ticket
successCriteria: I can fill shells in order - 2 in shell 1, 8 in shell 2, 8 in shell 3 - and write an arrangement such as 2,8,1
I can state the period from the number of shells and the group from the number of outer electrons
objectives.text: Use the electron arrangement to state an element's group and period

subject: science
title: Atomic structure and the periodic table
